subject.title: feat(agents): agent-owned gateway terminals with operator co-attach

question: Should agent terminal command and input execution inherit the existing exec approval policy, or become a separately opted-in unrestricted host-shell capability?
rationale: The patch intentionally creates a second RCE path with different authorization semantics; repository policy and tests cannot decide whether terminal enablement is meant to override an operator's existing exec deny or approval settings.

options.title: Reuse exec approvals
options.body: Require terminal commands and raw input that can execute shell actions to pass through the existing exec deny, allowlist, and approval contract.

options.title: Add explicit terminal opt-in
options.body: Keep direct terminal input only behind a separate agent-terminal permission with clear setup, upgrade, and security documentation.

options.title: Accept unrestricted owner terminals
options.body: Explicitly declare that enabling terminals grants unsandboxed owner agents direct host-shell execution regardless of exec approval settings.

recommendation.title: Reuse exec approvals
recommendation.body: Require terminal commands and raw input that can execute shell actions to pass through the existing exec deny, allowlist, and approval contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged Phase A infrastructure and the proposed terminal implementation, so they have the strongest feature-history context for presenting the security tradeoff.
